thread.title: Intraday Update: Dow Dips 80 Points Because Canada Is Still MIA on Nafta

author: Crystal Kim
title: Intraday Update: Dow Dips 80 Points Because Canada Is Still MIA on Nafta
text:
By Crystal Kim Aug. 31, 2018 1:10 p.m. ET Protect This House? Stocks slipped as Canada was still missing-in-action on the trade deal despite the White House-imposed Friday deadline. Concerns about protectionist policies are weighing on the Dow and to a lesser extent, the S&P 500. Those who can't handle the uncertainty are turning to fortune tellers . Ford Motor (F) could've used a crystal ball. The auto maker said Friday it would ditch plans to import a Made-in-China model due to tariffs. In today's Intraday Update , we...
Illustration: Drew Angerer/Getty Images •...don't think U.S. and Canada will complete a deal on a revised North American Free Trade Agreement;
•...see remarkable similarities between the S&P 500's current moves and how its early 1990s grooves;
•...note that Ford Motor (F) isn't the only company suffering tariffs.
Mi Casa (No) Es Su Casa Stocks are stalling as investors wait in vain to see if Canada and U.S. will make nice on NAFTA. The Dow has fallen 80 points, or 0.3%, to 25,900.22, and the S&P 500 has slipped 0.2% to 2893.90. Meanwhile the Nasdaq Composite is roughly flat but in positive territory at 8090.96.
While protectionist concerns seem to be Friday's focus, three tariff canaries are sending mixed messages. Caterpillar (CAT) is up 0.3%, 3M (MMM) is moving sideways, and Walmart (WMT) is down 0.9%. "Developed market equities have generally taken the escalation of U.S.-China trade tensions since mid-June in their stride. The effects have only really been obvious in relatively small sub-sectors who are most exposed to protectionism like car producers," writes John Higgins of Capital Economics . If President Donald Trump does plow ahead with plans to impose tariffs on $200 billion of Chinese imports, emerging markets' stocks could feel the pain he adds. Later, those tariffs may start weighing on U.S. stocks, too, as China begins targeting multinationals. Not to mention, there's oil to worry about. Tariffs are the wrong response to China as my colleague Matt Klein pointed out in June.
US President Donald Trump Illustration: Brendan Smialowski/Getty Images This half-Nafta should be dubbed "hafta" as in corporations don't hafta pack it up and go home, but in this political environment that seems like the only option.
While President Trump is attempting to protect this house (the U.S.), he may lose another – the House of Representatives. "All the experts I know tell me the House will fall, but those same folks told me Trump would never be President!," writes Raymond James ' Jeff Saut . That said, even if the House "falls" to the Democrats, Saut doesn't think much will change, because even President Barack Obama said: "I have a pen and a phone." DJT is no different.
The S&P 500's moves may give one a sense of déjà vu. Tom McClellan , author of the eponymous newsletter, noted that stocks are moving in Trump's first term the way they did during President Bill Clinton 's first term. Take a look:
"The first two years of [Clinton's] term in office were marked by numerous scandals, and by a stock market which saw a scary dip in the 2nd year, which eventually resolved itself...At the time, the Federal Reserve was commencing a program of rate hikes, which had market participants worried," wrote McClellan. He also noted that Nafta got settled in January 1994 at "exactly the right time in the rhyme and meter of history."
If history is any indication, then the next quarter will be rough, but will lead to another rally come 2019.
Midday Movers Apple (AAPL) is up 0.9% at $227.18 ahead of its iPhone event on Sep. 12, but the event may not make the stock move as it once has .
Cooper (COO) is down 3.7% to $253.98 after the medical-device maker reported poorer-than-expected earnings. It reported $3.00 in earnings per share for the quarter, but analysts expected the company to earn $3.07.
Ford Motor (F) is down 2% at $9.51 after the auto maker said it would ditch plans to import a China-built small car citing tariffs.
Illustration: Lav Ulv Goodyear Tire & Rubber (GT) is down 3.9% to $22.77 after Germany-based Berenberg Bank cut its rating for the auto-parts firm to Hold from Buy.
HCA Healthcare (HCA) is up 1.3% to $133.10 as the health-care services provider agreed to buy Mission Health , a nonprofit based in North Carolina, for some $1.5 billion.
